clusters.label: Electrons
clusters.definition: Electronic charge carriers contributing to electrical transport.
clusters.reason: Both explicitly identify electrons as charge carriers; their material environments and relative contributions remain claim-specific.

clusters.label: Film optical properties
clusters.definition: Optical characteristics of films affected by preparation or composition.
clusters.reason: Both labels denote the same broad property category, without identifying distinct optical subtypes; film compositions remain attached to their claims.

clusters.label: Ferromagnetic ordering (DFT prediction)
clusters.definition: Ferromagnetic ordering predicted for the investigated Ce3XY inverse cubic perovskites, with X = Al or In and Y = C or N.
clusters.reason: The ordering is explicitly a result of a DFT study.

clusters.label: Ferromagnetic ordering (experimental observation)
clusters.definition: Ferromagnetic ordering below the Curie temperature in Ni-substituted PrCo1-xNixO3 samples, inferred from magnetic measurements.
clusters.reason: ZFC/FC curves and magnetic hysteresis support experimentally observed ordering, distinct from the other member's prediction.

clusters.label: Closed band gap
clusters.definition: An electronic structure state in which the band gap has closed.
clusters.reason: Both electronic-structure calculations identify gap closure; dopants, compositions and the resulting conduction details remain claim-specific.

clusters.label: Electron tunnelling
clusters.definition: The low-temperature electron tunnelling transport process identified in ferrites at 4 K < T < 35 K.
clusters.reason: All describe the same tunnelling process, separately from electron hopping and ionic relaxation; Ni and Ga affect that process in different samples.

clusters.label: Heat-carrying acoustic phonons
clusters.definition: Acoustic phonons that transport heat through a crystal lattice.
clusters.reason: All identify the same phonon category interacting with or being scattered by low-energy vibrational modes; specific materials and interactions remain separate claims.

clusters.label: Significant lattice anharmonicity
clusters.definition: Pronounced anharmonic character of crystal-lattice vibrations.
clusters.reason: Both denote the same lattice property associated with bonding hierarchy; the Tl+ rattling and copper–iodine antibonding explanations remain distinct contextual mechanisms.

clusters.label: Three-dimensional framework of P–P-linked SiP4 tetrahedra
clusters.definition: The framework formed by P–P bonds connecting SiP4 tetrahedra in Sr2SiP4 and Eu2SiP4.
clusters.reason: The member denotes a chemically specified tetrahedral framework.

clusters.label: Three-dimensional framework of corrugated layers and {SbSe}8 ribbons
clusters.definition: The framework in FePb4Sb6Se14 formed by connected corrugated layers and {SbSe}8 ribbons, containing cylindrical voids parallel to [100].
clusters.reason: Its building blocks, connectivity and chemical composition distinguish it from the SiP4 framework; shared dimensionality does not establish identity.

clusters.label: Curie temperature
clusters.definition: The temperature marking the transition between magnetically ordered and paramagnetic states.
clusters.reason: Both denote the same transition-temperature quantity; substitution effects and numerical temperatures belong to individual material claims.

clusters.label: n-type semiconductor character
clusters.definition: Semiconducting character associated with electron-type majority carriers.
clusters.reason: All explicitly identify n-type semiconductor character; temperature, composition limits and minority sample exceptions remain claim-specific.

clusters.label: High crystallinity
clusters.definition: A high degree of crystalline order in a material.
clusters.reason: Both denote the same structural descriptor, with no distinct crystallinity subtype specified; sample identities and evidence strength remain separate.

clusters.label: Poor reflectivity
clusters.definition: Low optical reflectivity reported in first-principles studies.
clusters.reason: Both describe low reflectivity from DFT studies, without specifying different reflectivity subtypes.

clusters.label: Semiconductor character
clusters.definition: Semiconducting electronic character associated with an electronic band gap.
clusters.reason: Both electronic-structure descriptions establish semiconductor character; specific gaps, magnetic states and orbital contributions remain claim-specific.

clusters.label: Dominant ionic conduction
clusters.definition: A transport regime in which ionic conduction is the dominant contribution.
clusters.reason: Both denote ionic dominance; different oxygen-pressure conditions and the tentative attribution in titania do not define different conduction concepts.

clusters.label: Grains
clusters.definition: Crystalline grain regions contributing to electrical transport or relaxation within a sample.
clusters.reason: Both refer to grain contributions in electrical-response analysis; the second explicitly distinguishes these from grain-boundary contributions.

clusters.label: p-type semiconductor character
clusters.definition: Semiconducting character associated with hole-type majority carriers.
clusters.reason: Both explicitly identify p-type semiconductor character; composition restrictions and band-gap values remain attached to their respective claims.

clusters.label: EuLaCuSe3
clusters.definition: The quaternary selenide with composition EuLaCuSe3.
clusters.reason: The identical explicit composition establishes material identity; decomposition and crystallographic results describe complementary properties.

clusters.label: Bond strength
clusters.definition: The strength of chemical bonding in the investigated compounds.
clusters.reason: Both denote bond strength itself, with pressure-induced enhancement expressed by relations; the particular bond species and bonding characters remain claim-specific.

clusters.label: Verwey transition near 125 K
clusters.definition: The characteristic magnetite-related Verwey transition near 125 K discussed in substituted ferrites.
clusters.reason: Both explicitly identify the same transition; Ni and Ga substitutions and their suppression thresholds describe distinct effects on it.

clusters.label: Superconducting Tc
clusters.definition: The critical temperature of the superconducting transition.
clusters.reason: Both denote the same transition-temperature quantity; proposed links to anharmonicity, localization and band structure remain separate hypotheses.
